findings.evidence: Host tools. Bash below means the host's shell tool; AskUserQuestion (with multiSelect) means its structured-question tool; Read means its file reader.
findings.fix: Keep only the fallback: if the host has no structured-question tool, number the options and wait. Drop the restatement of what Bash, AskUserQuestion and Read are.

findings.evidence: python3 -c " ... kept_clis = {<CLI names the user kept>} ... chosen = {<cli>: [<chosen model id(s)>], ...}
findings.fix: Replace the inline python3 -c template with a complete runnable snippet, or route the filter through an existing ai-kit-spec.py subcommand, so the agent does not have to invent the JSON rewrite.

findings.evidence: ## NEVER lists fourteen rules, but there is no Gotchas section for environment facts that are not already a NEVER item.
findings.fix: Add a short Gotchas section for facts that defy assumptions and are not already NEVER rules, such as a fresh shell per Bash call and probe-quota merging local and global keys.

findings.evidence: Description covers WHAT, WHEN and keywords, but trigger query 6 still says 'global review-spec file' while the description only names config.toml and an old review-spec.toml migration.
findings.fix: Cross-AI lane setup: detects installed CLIs and models, asks which to use for review and execute lanes and in what priority order, then writes the [lanes] table of ai-kit's config.toml. Writes the per-project ./.aikit/config.toml by default (always announces the exact path), asks before replacing an existing [lanes] table (local or global), and migrates an old review-spec.toml on first use. Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup, asks to write or migrate a review-spec or reviewer roster, or when ai-kit-spec-review warns no config exists, even if they say review-spec instead of config.toml. Supports --check-only (report availability, no writes), --local (force local write without asking), and --global (force the user ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/ai-kit/config.toml directly). Not for running a review, editing another table, or writing secrets.

findings.evidence: cli-model-selection.md is 344 lines and is loaded in full whenever any CLI is kept, including the ranking script and catalog-write JSON that only some branches need.
findings.fix: Keep the 8-item order in that file and move the ranking python3 -c block and the confirm-catalog JSON template into a second reference loaded only when unmatched entries exist or ranking starts.

findings.evidence: Never write to the global config without asking — unless --global or --local was explicitly passed. Step 2.1 says --global forces the user config directly, skipping the ask, while the replacement gate still asks before replacing an existing roster.
findings.fix: Change the NEVER bullet to: never write the global file without an explicit --global or a Step 2.1 'replace' answer, and never treat --global or --local as consent to replace an existing roster.

findings.evidence: Nine should-trigger and eight should-not-trigger queries; the negatives are unrelated tasks (unit tests, rebase, README, make test), not near-misses such as running a review or editing a non-lanes table.
findings.fix: Replace at least four negatives with near-misses: run a cross-AI review, edit [runner] or [hooks], write secrets.env, and trust an already-written local config without changing lanes.

findings.evidence: Eight cases have prompts and assertions, but assertions are agent-behavior checks ('Runs detect-runtimes before asking') with empty files on seven of eight cases, so they are not graded against an artifact.
findings.fix: Add expected config.toml or report text for at least the replace, migration and unconfirmed-read-only cases, and assert on that output rather than only on which subcommand ran.

findings.evidence: The global prompt says 'Migrates my old review-spec.toml roster to the new config.toml,' but Step 2.1 only migrates when replacing a roster or when no roster exists; a check-only run reports 'migration pending' and writes nothing. There is no branch that migrates without a full lane rewrite.
findings.fix: State at Step 2.1 that a migrate-only request is not this wizard's write: report migration pending and point at the next command that reads the roster, unless the user also asked to replace the lanes.

findings.evidence: Step 3 says the global target is used because the user picked 'replace the existing global config' at Step 2, while Step 2.1's actual option is 'replace the global roster?'
findings.fix: Use the Step 2.1 option text in Step 3 so the agent matches the answer it actually collected.
